accepted_edits.reason: the s25 rewrite and s24 sentence removal are exactly what findings done_when-1, reasoning-1 and reasoning-2 of r-20261116T071134426667 asked for

findings.reason: as written the fail-first gate is green at base, so the node would ship a test that proves nothing, or discover the contradiction mid-build and lose a round.
findings.text: s25's red criterion is "a follower that cannot open the station store, while the station's beat is fresh and its tick is running, draws no lost row and offers no re-arm, whatever the snapshot's age", but at base a fresh exported beat already draws nothing: with an exported station-snapshot.json whose heartbeat is the current instant and TMPDIR pointed at a directory with no station store, ProducerSnapshotNotices.poll returned `[]` (reproduction kept at repro-s25-fresh-beat.log, module reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py at base c6f9f10f), while the cited field row is drawn only when that exported beat has aged: a 206s heartbeat returned `producer imas-codex lost: snapshot age 206s exceeds 120s; re-arm with: reckon crew watch --ensure ...` (bands STATION_STALE_SECONDS = FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECONDS = 120, watch_unit.py:1094-1122)

findings.reason: the section's stated input cannot exist for the follower it names, so a worker reading the code would either contradict the plan or invent a different endpoint.
findings.text: s25's Why states that the exported snapshot "carries the heartbeat and nothing about a running tick" and that only the store answers the tick, and its own docstring in the base agrees (`read_station_answer` marks an off-node reading as stopped-or-live and "never claims a progress it cannot see"), so the follower that cannot open the store has no way to observe "the station's beat is fresh and its tick is running"; the endpoint must instead require the exported reading to carry the station's live tick so that a follower whose exported beat has aged past the window reads the station as slow rather than lost

findings.reason: the write paths and done-when already scope the worker off the moved mechanism, so the leftover sentence costs a confused read, not a wrong node.
findings.text: s24's Why still ends with "the watch drawing one `limit` row per follower: two identical rows at 23:25:53 and 23:25:55 for one reset", evidence for the deliverable that moved to s27, while s24's write paths no longer include reckon/crew/ticker.py
